extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners and patent applicants/attorneys handling national-security and PCT/international filing issues
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for screening, handling, prosecution, correspondence, petitions, and public access rules for patent applications subject to national security review, secrecy orders, and PCT/international-file handling at the USPTO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality of international preliminary examination reports (IPER)
rubrics_metrics.description: Neither the International Bureau nor the International Preliminary Examining Authority shall, unless requested or authorized by the applicant, give information on the issuance or non-issuance of an international preliminary examination report and on the withdrawal or non-withdrawal of the demand or of any election.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not disclose issuance/non-issuance of IPER or withdrawal status unless applicant requests or authorizes such disclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Secrecy of international applications when foreign filing/license refused
rubrics_metrics.description: If a license to file in a foreign country is refused or if an international application is ordered to be kept secret and a permit refused, the Patent and Trademark Office, when acting as a Receiving Office, International Searching Authority, or International Preliminary Examining Authority, may not disclose the contents of such application to anyone not authorized to receive such disclosure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain strict non-disclosure of application contents in these circumstances; restrict dissemination to authorized recipients only.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditions for furnishing copies of international application files (37 CFR 1.14(g)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: Copies of international application files (Home Copy, Search Copy, Examination Copy) designating the U.S. and published in accordance with PCT Article 21(2) will be furnished upon written request showing publication and U.S. designation and upon payment of appropriate fee, subject to specific role-based conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Home Copy: provided if international application was filed with U.S. Receiving Office. Search Copy: provided if U.S. acted as International Searching Authority, but written opinion unavailable until 30 months from priority date. Examination Copy: provided only if U.S. acted as IPEA, an IPER has issued, and the U.S. was elected. Requests must meet PCT Articles 30/38 and Rules 94.2/94.3 requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provision of English translations of international publications (37 CFR 1.14(g)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: A copy of an English language translation of a publication of an international application filed in the USPTO pursuant to 35 U.S.C. 154(d)(4) will be furnished upon written request showing publication and U.S. designation and upon payment of fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: USPTO will not notify the public generally of such translations; applicants remain responsible for notifying potential infringers to obtain provisional rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Access to international application files under PCT rules (37 CFR 1.14(g)(3) and (4))
rubrics_metrics.description: Access to international application files or copies will be permitted in accordance with PCT Articles and Rules (including Rules 44ter.1, 94.2, 94.3) after international publication; copies of the application-as-filed will not be provided prior to international publication under PCT Article 21(2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not provide application-as-filed prior to publication. Follow PCT and 37 CFR procedures for when and how third parties may access files.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination copy access prohibition (PCT Article 38 / 37 CFR 1.14(g)(5))
rubrics_metrics.description: Access to the Examination Copy of an international application is prohibited in accordance with PCT Article 38.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not permit public access to Examination Copies; follow exceptions only as provided by statute/regulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request formality for copies of international files
rubrics_metrics.description: Requests for copies of an international application file must be in written form sent to the Office of PCT Legal Administration, include a showing that the application has been published and that the U.S. was designated (preferably the front page of the published application), and be accompanied by the appropriate fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure completeness of requests (publication evidence + designation + fee) and direct them to the specified office to avoid denial/delay.

rubrics_metrics.name: USPTO post-publication access to international files
rubrics_metrics.description: After publication under 35 U.S.C. 122(b), the USPTO will make available copies of international application files kept by the USPTO and allow access to those files in accordance with 37 CFR 1.14(a) and related provisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Once published and USPTO-held, copies/access are governed by 1.14 procedures; differentiate between files kept by USPTO and Examination Copies withheld under PCT Article 38.

rubrics_metrics.name: Screening for national security and referral to agencies (35 U.S.C. 181/35 U.S.C. 184)
rubrics_metrics.description: All provisional, nonprovisional, and PCT international applications received in the USPTO are screened upon receipt for subject matter that might impact national security and are referred to appropriate agencies for consideration of restrictions on disclosure or foreign filing license.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Designated personnel perform initial screening; examiners must also be alert for sensitive subject matter and forward candidate applications to Licensing & Review with significant subject matter identified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling applications where government has property interest or invention made outside U.S.
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications on inventions made outside the U.S. and those where a U.S. Government defense agency has a property interest will not be made available to defense agencies; certain licensing requirements limit review under 35 U.S.C. 181 to inventions made in the U.S.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize jurisdictional limitations and different treatment for foreign-made inventions and government-property-interest cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptance and handling of national security classified documents (37 CFR 5.1(c),(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent applications and documents that are national security classified and contain authorized national security markings are accepted by the Office but must be hand-carried to Licensing and Review or mailed as prescribed; the applicant must obtain a secrecy order or provide authority to cancel the markings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not accept classified documents via regular public channels; ensure compliance with routing, handling protocols, and time periods to avoid abandonment if notification/clearance is not provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withholding publication/allowance while under national security review (37 CFR 5.1(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: An application will not be published under § 1.211 or allowed under § 1.311 if publication or disclosure would be detrimental to national security. An application under national security review will not be published at least until six months from its filing date or three months from the date it was referred to a defense agency, whichever is later. Classified applications will not be published or allowed until declassified and any secrecy order rescinded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Delay publication/allowance as specified; coordinate with Licensing & Review and the referring agency for timing and declassification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Issuance of secrecy orders (37 CFR 5.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: When notified by the chief officer of a defense agency that publication or disclosure would be detrimental to national security, an order that the invention be kept secret will be issued by the Commissioner for Patents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Secrecy orders are issued on agency notification. Compensation claims connected to secrecy orders must be made to the issuing agency, not the PTO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of secrecy orders to related subject matter (37 CFR 5.2(c); Related subject matter)
rubrics_metrics.description: A secrecy order applies to any application disclosing any significant part of the subject matter of an application under secrecy order; subsequently filed applications containing significant part of that subject matter also fall within the scope and must be brought to Licensing & Review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monitor related or overlapping filings and promptly notify Licensing & Review; hand-carry or route accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prosecution limitations and procedures under secrecy order (37 CFR 5.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Prosecution continues while under secrecy order to specified points: final rejections must be prosecuted/appealed to avoid abandonment though hearings are not set until the secrecy order is removed; interferences generally will not be declared; when found in condition for allowance except for the secrecy order the case is placed in suspension and applicant/agency are notified; international applications under secrecy order will not be transmitted to international authorities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow statutory reply periods (often full period set); appeals must be completed even if hearing withheld; recognize suspension mechanics and restricted international transmission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition for rescission of secrecy order (37 CFR 5.4)
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition for rescission may be filed by any principal affected and must recite all facts purported to render the order ineffectual (including full data and copies of alleged prior publications/patents), identify any government contract relevant to subject matter, and be filed in duplicate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide complete factual support (publications, patents, contracts); appeal to Secretary of Commerce may be taken only after petition denial within specified timelines (appeal within 60 days).

rubrics_metrics.name: Permit or modification to disclose or file abroad (37 CFR 5.5)
rubrics_metrics.description: Consent to disclosure or filing abroad is by permit or modification of the secrecy order. Petitions must fully recite reason/purpose, identify proposed disclosees and their security clearances (including agency and degree/date), list all countries and attorneys where filing is proposed, and vouch for loyalty/integrity of disclosees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For foreign filing petitions include complete list of countries and agents and clearance details; organizations may petition for general permits for routine repeated disclosures but must ordinarily show sufficient clearance for highest classification involved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of Secrecy Orders and their scope
rubrics_metrics.description: Three types: (A) Secrecy Order and Permit for Foreign Filing in Certain Countries — for export-controlled technical data (DoD Directive/ MCTL) and identifies countries where filing permitted; (B) Secrecy Order and Permit for Disclosing Classified Information — for properly classified/classifiable technical data where owner has DD Form 441 (treat as classified material with notification of classification level); (C) Secrecy Order — for technical data classifiable where owner lacks DoD Security Agreement (prevents disclosure unless express written consent).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Type A intended to permit filing in reciprocal-security countries (list provided); Type B treats application as classified and includes classification level; Type C used when other types don't apply; permits (e.g., Permit A) may relax restrictions. Note EPO central filing is not permitted under some orders — must file in individual member states as identified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Secrecy order effects and correspondence restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: A secrecy order restricts disclosure/publication of the invention in any form and requires that correspondence related to the subject matter be transmitted so as to preclude disclosure to unauthorized individuals. Subject matter under secrecy order must be safeguarded and not placed in public records until declassified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not use facsimile transmission for such correspondence per 37 CFR 1.6(d)(6); ensure mailing/hand-carrying to Licensing & Review; changes in power of attorney must include identifying data for security clearances; ensure correspondence address is suitable for receipt of security information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation to notify disclosees and report inadvertent disclosures
rubrics_metrics.description: If any significant part of the subject matter has been revealed to any U.S. citizen in the U.S., principals must promptly inform that person of the secrecy order and penalties. If revealed to foreign persons or in foreign countries, principals must not inform the disclosee but must promptly furnish details (date, disclosee name/address, identification of subject matter, any U.S. government authorization to export) to Mail Stop L&R.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow reporting procedures precisely and provide identification of any related foreign patent filings if applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duration and renewal of secrecy orders
rubrics_metrics.description: Under 35 U.S.C. 181 a secrecy order remains in effect for 1 year from issuance and may be renewed for additional periods not exceeding 1 year upon agency notice. Expiration or failure to renew does not relieve principals of responsibilities for classified subject matter unless expressly declassified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monitor renewal notices and maintain security measures until formal declassification and removal of markings is authorized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling of papers bearing security markings
rubrics_metrics.description: Papers marked per Executive Orders and showing agency-applied markings are accepted in patent applications but must be referred to Technology Center Working Group 3640 for clarification/security treatment. Such items must not be placed in public records until markings are declassified or explained.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authorized markings may appear on drawings provided outside illustrations and must be removed upon declassification; promptly refer any items with 'Secret'/'Confidential' markings to TC WG 3640.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination location and special processing for Secrecy Order cases
rubrics_metrics.description: All applications with a Secrecy Order are examined in Technology Center Working Group 3640 and Art Unit 3662. If the Order is imposed after docketing elsewhere, the case will be transferred. Secrecy order cases are examined for patentability but may not be passed to issue while under order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests by other examiners for interference searches involving classified/Secrecy Order cases should be handled by TC WG 3640/Art Unit 3662 examiners; follow transfer and processing rules strictly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination practice adjustments for Secrecy Order cases
rubrics_metrics.description: Due to administrative burdens, full statutory reply periods will ordinarily be set for Office actions on Secrecy Order cases. Amendments received after a notice of allowability (Form D-10 closing prosecution) are not entered until the secrecy order is rescinded; at that time free-from-objection amendments will be entered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Set full reply periods, withhold entry of post-allowability amendments until rescission, and upon rescission process or deny entry consistent with normal practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to seek order or declassification when markings are present
rubrics_metrics.description: When applications bear national security markings but no Secrecy Order, the examiner should require the applicant to seek imposition of a Secrecy Order or authority to cancel the markings, preferably with the first action and prior to final disposition. If no Secrecy Order issues, the Office will set a time period within which the applicant must either obtain an order, declassify, or submit evidence of a good faith effort to obtain an order to avoid abandonment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Promptly prompt applicants to resolve marking status; failure to act within set periods risks abandonment. Evidence of good faith effort can temporarily stave off abandonment if submitted timely.
